big: Meena's car hits a scooter. The scooter rider needs treatment and her bike needs repair. Her own car is barely scratched. Which of her covers pays for whom?

lines: The law says I must have motor insurance. Is that the whole thing?
The law requires third-party cover, which pays for harm you cause to others. Own damage cover for your own vehicle is optional, and is usually worth having.

rows: Compulsory. Pays for injury or damage you cause to others
Pays for your own vehicle's damage, fire or theft
The vehicle's agreed value, the most paid if it is stolen or written off
A premium discount for each year without a claim
note: IDV falls as the vehicle ages. Setting it too low lowers the premium but also what you can get back.

title: Motor insurance
stops: Own damage cover is compulsory in every case
IDV is the agreed value of the vehicle
A no-claim bonus is lost in the very first year
caps: The law requires third-party cover for every vehicle on the road.
Own damage cover is optional, though most people choose it.
IDV is the maximum payout for theft or a total loss.
The bonus grows with each year in which you make no claim.

q: Rohan's car damages another person's car in an accident that was his fault. Which cover pays for the other car?
why: Own damage cover is for his own vehicle and not for others.
A no-claim bonus is a discount on the premium and is not a payout.
IDV is the agreed value of his own car, used for theft and total loss.
Third-party cover pays for harm caused to others by his vehicle.

q: Meena's car is stolen. What decides the most she can get back?
opts: The price of fuel in that month
The number of seats in the car itself
The colour that she chose for it
why: Fuel prices have no link to the amount paid for a stolen car.
The IDV is the agreed value, and it is the most paid for theft or total loss.
Seats do not decide the payout. The agreed value does.
Colour does not decide what the policy pays for a stolen car.

q: Rohan has not made any claim for two years. What does he usually gain at renewal?
opts: A higher deductible without any choice
A bigger bill for the same cover
why: A no-claim bonus lowers the premium after a year with no claim.
A bonus does not push the deductible up unless he chooses.
A record with no claims does not make the bill any bigger.
Having no claims does not end a policy in any way.

q: Meena sets her car's IDV much lower to save on the premium. What is the risk?
opts: The cover becomes compulsory by law
The third-party cover stops at once
Her no-claim bonus is cancelled too
why: Cover does not become compulsory by the IDV she sets.
Third-party cover is a legal requirement and is not changed by IDV.
A lower IDV cuts the premium, but it also lowers the most she can receive.
An IDV choice does not cancel a no-claim bonus.

pts: Third-party cover is compulsory. Own damage cover is a choice.
IDV is the agreed value, and the most paid for theft or total loss.
A no-claim bonus is a discount for each year with no claim.
